content:
Here is a reasonably literal English translation of the text. A few lines are damaged or uncertain, so I have marked unclear portions with brackets or ellipses.

1. **From day to day, from heaven and earth it was created.**  
2. **From night to night, from heaven and earth it was created.**  
3. **From the name, from fate it was decreed.**  
4. **The Anuna gods were born therefrom.**  
5. **The goddess Inana obtained the NIR.PA fate.**  
6. **The goddess Inana made heaven and earth tremble.**  
7. **The goddess Inana […] gave birth and engendered.**  
8. **The gods of abundance fastened [it] to the “A X X” one’s [storehouse?].**  
9. **The countless gods perform labor; the small gods carry the [building] basket.**  
10. **The gods press and pile up the riverbank; they heap up the earth.**  
11. **The gods spread out the clay; they determine its life and establish its word.**  
12. **At that time, broad understanding, wisdom, was present among the numerous gods.**  
13. **Enki, in the Apsu, in the marshes and canals, whose heart no god can fathom,**  
14. **whose resting place none can enter,**  
15. **whose gods perform tasks in the underworld, and whose shrines are present in abundance,**  
16. **for a person who lies down in darkness, whose resting place cannot be awakened,**  
17. **for Namma, the mother who bore the great offspring, for the numerous gods,**  
18. **she brought her tears to the gods, to her children.**  
19. **They slept with him there, and they lay with him there.**  
20. **[...], not letting him rise.**  
21. **The creator-god has made your hand; the work of your hand [...]; they touch / graze against his neck.**

If you want, I can also provide:
- a **more polished literary translation**, or
- a **line-by-line grammatical breakdown** of the Sumerian.
